coreIdea: Minimum states = number of distinct 'residual behaviors' to remember. Modular condition (div by k) = k states. Combined independent conditions = product of moduli.
mustRememberFormulas: 'mod p AND mod q' (independent) → p×q states
'last k symbols matter' → O(2^k) states typically
NFA n states → minimal DFA ≤2^n (upper bound only, not exact)
Complement of L needs the SAME state count as L

commonTrapsQuickList: Always verify product-construction state counts for unreachable/equivalent states — p×q is an upper bound too, not always exact
Complement needs SAME state count as original, not different
2^n is only an upper bound for NFA→DFA, no simple universal lower bound
Minimal DFA is UNIQUE for any given regular language
highYieldPyqLessons: State-counting (18/25) is nearly the whole topic — build fluency with modular/product/sliding-window counting until it's automatic.
This topic pairs perfectly with Regular Language's Myhill-Nerode content — study them close together.
